1	# Market
2	
3	The competitive landscape for Claudinite: the open substrate standards every
4	coding-agent user already has on disk, the platform-native layer Anthropic now
5	ships itself, the direct rule-sync competitors, the adjacent content
6	ecosystems, and the enterprise vendors encroaching from above. Business models
7	and price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); customer
8	segments in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md); what this means for
9	Claudinite in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).
10	
11	## Key insights
12	
13	- Anthropic ships the session half natively, but CLI auto-install of org-mandated plugins was closed "not planned."
14	- Nobody converges repos: no auto-PR loop from a canon, no CI convention gates; native auto memory is machine-local, never shared.
15	- Rival enforcement is config-drift only: they check the rules arrived; nothing checks the rules are followed.
16	- The rule-sync category is nearly all free OSS under 3k stars; the one hosted SaaS (rulesync.dev) is in free beta.
17	- Enterprise scorecard vendors (Cortex, Port, OpsLevel) now sell AI-agent governance from above; OpsLevel's Tidra ships auto-PRs.
18	- Anthropic's own docs say CLAUDE.md is "context, not enforced configuration" — the vendor states Claudinite's premise.
19	- The AGENTS.md request (4,944 👍) was closed *completed* on 2026-08-17 by shipping an import; Claude Code still won't read the file.
20	
21	## The substrate: per-repo convention files
22	
23	Every agent-facing repo already carries at least one plain-text convention
24	file, and Claudinite has to interoperate with all of them rather than compete
25	with them:
26	
27	- **AGENTS.md** is the vendor-neutral standard: a plain-markdown,
28	  no-frontmatter file at the repo root, formalized as an open spec in August
29	  2025 and donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) on
30	  December 9, 2025 — alongside MCP and Block's goose, with AWS, Anthropic,
31	  Google, Microsoft and OpenAI as platinum members — citing adoption by more
32	  than 60,000 open-source projects.
33	  *Correction (2026-07-31):* this page previously said "read by 30+ agents,"
34	  citing the codersera guide; that page actually says "native support in 20+
35	  tools," and the "30+" figure appears to have been conflated with Ruler's
36	  own supported-agent marketing. The scale citation is now the LF
37	  announcement (primary).
38	- The spec itself is deliberately minimal — "a README for agents," no
39	  required fields, no schema — and says nothing about enforcement, machine
40	  checks, versioning, or packaged conventions. The only shared semantics are
41	  precedence (nearest file wins; chat instructions override). Enforcement and
42	  packaging are out of scope, i.e. open territory.
43	- **CLAUDE.md** is Claude Code's project-memory file, now a four-level
44	  hierarchy (managed policy / user / project / local) plus path-scoped
45	  `.claude/rules/` files and `@path` imports. Claude Code still reads
46	  CLAUDE.md natively, not AGENTS.md — the docs recommend an `@AGENTS.md`
47	  import or symlink as the bridge. Community best practice still converges on
48	  keeping it under ~200 lines (spot-checked 2026-07-31: the cited guide is
49	  alive and still says this).
50	- **The AGENTS.md request was closed as completed on 2026-08-17 — and Claude
51	  Code still does not read the file** (researched 2026-08-21).
52	  `anthropics/claude-code` #6235 "Feature Request: Support AGENTS.md." was
53	  closed `completed` by the Claude Code lead (bcherny) at 2026-08-17T03:37Z,
54	  after twelve months and 4,944 👍 (6,367 total reactions, 374 comments) —
55	  the largest quantified demand signal in the agent-config space, and now
56	  answered by an *import*, not by native reading. The memory doc, re-fetched
57	  the same day the issue's last update landed, still says flatly "Claude Code
58	  reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`"; what shipped is `/import` (Claude Code
59	  v2.1.213+), which "appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as
60	  `AGENTS.md` to the matching `CLAUDE.md`", alongside `/init` under
61	  `CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1` reading AGENTS.md at generation time. Both are
62	  one-time copies into CLAUDE.md — the same bridge this wiki has recorded
63	  since 2026-08-02, now blessed as the official answer. The read gap is
64	  therefore *durable by decision*, not by backlog: the interop whitespace
65	  stays open, and a copy-in bridge is itself a drift source, which is the
66	  territory Claudinite is already in.
67	- **Anthropic now states the enforcement gap in its own docs, in Claudinite's
68	  own terms** (primary page, 2026-08-21). The memory doc's opening comparison
69	  says of CLAUDE.md and auto memory: "Claude treats them as context, not
70	  enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude
71	  decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead," and its managed-policy section
72	  draws the same line: "Settings rules are enforced by the client regardless
73	  of what Claude decides to do. CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's
74	  behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer." The same page tells teams
75	  to "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file" because "longer files
76	  consume more context and reduce adherence." The platform vendor is the
77	  primary source for the premise the whole rule-sync category is built on
78	  top of and never addresses.
79	- **Auto memory is the native learning loop — and it is machine-local by
80	  design.** Claude Code writes its own notes from a user's corrections into
81	  `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`, on by default. The doc is explicit
82	  that "Auto memory is machine-local... Files are not shared across machines
83	  or cloud environments" (primary page, 2026-08-21), and only the first 200
84	  lines / 25KB of its index load per session. Nothing native promotes a
85	  lesson from one machine to a team, a repo, or a fleet.
86	- **SKILL.md / Agent Skills** became a cross-vendor open standard: Anthropic
87	  published the spec (agentskills.io, Dec 2025), and by mid-2026 roughly 40
88	  tools — OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, JetBrains
89	  Junie, Block's goose — read the same format. anthropics/skills sits at
90	  ~165.3k stars (verified via GitHub API 2026-07-31). The spec mandates only
91	  `name`/`description` frontmatter; nothing about checks or distribution.
92	- **Cursor** keeps its `.cursor/rules/` directory; Cursor Teams now also
93	  markets "Team Commands" with a team baseline and drift detection — the
94	  platform vendor absorbing single-tool rule sharing natively.
95	- **GitHub Copilot** keeps `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and reads
96	  AGENTS.md; GitHub's own blog mined 2,500+ AGENTS.md files for guidance.
97	
98	None of these substrate formats answer the question Claudinite is for: how
99	the *same* convention, once refined, reaches every repo that shares it,
100	stays current there, and is *checked* rather than trusted.
101	
102	## The platform layer: what Claude Code now ships natively
103	
104	The largest competitive change since this page was seeded is Anthropic's own
105	distribution stack (all verified against current Claude Code docs,
106	2026-07-31):
107	
108	- **Plugins** (announced October 9, 2025) bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP
109	  servers, LSP servers, and default settings into versioned packages,
110	  distributed through decentralized **marketplaces** (`marketplace.json` in
111	  any git repo/npm source, semver or SHA pinning, background auto-update).
112	- **Plugins can be centrally mandated — but not uniformly across surfaces.**
113	  Project-level `extraKnownMarketplaces`/`enabledPlugins`, managed-settings
114	  force-enable, `strictKnownMarketplaces` lockdown, container seed dirs, and
115	  claude.ai org-level plugin sync on Team/Enterprise plans (per-plugin
116	  installation preferences — Installed by default / Available for install /
117	  Required / Not available) all exist as mechanisms.
118	  *Correction (2026-08-09):* this page previously left the impression the
119	  CLI itself honors `enabledPlugins`/`extraKnownMarketplaces` automatically.
120	  It doesn't. [anthropics/claude-code#45323](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/45323)
121	  ("CLI: Auto-install plugins from org managed settings") documents that the
122	  CLI fetches the managed-settings marketplace into
123	  `~/.claude/remote-settings.json` at startup but never registers it in
124	  `known_marketplaces.json` or installs the listed plugin — the org's admin
125	  still has to have every user run `/plugin marketplace add` and
126	  `/plugin install` by hand, or bake plugins into a container image at build
127	  time via `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`. Filed April 2026, the issue was
128	  closed **"not planned."** The same managed settings *do* auto-install on
129	  the desktop and web apps per the issue's own comparison and the Claude
130	  Help Center's org-plugin-management article (that page egress-blocked to
131	  this pass's fetcher — via search-quoted context, not opened directly) — so
132	  the CLI, Claudinite's own delivery surface, is specifically the one where
133	  central mandate still isn't unattended.
134	- **Managed settings** give admins non-overridable org-wide permission rules,
135	  hooks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), MCP allowlists, model restrictions, and
136	  even an org-wide CLAUDE.md blob — delivered by MDM, machine-wide.
137	- **Hooks** provide deterministic in-session blocking (exit code 2 /
138	  `permissionDecision: "deny"`); Anthropic's own docs route enforcement away
139	  from prose to hooks — validating Claudinite's thesis while shipping the
140	  session-side half of it.
141	- **Native scheduling** arrived in three tiers (session cron//loop, cloud
142	  Routines, Desktop tasks); **auto memory** is per-project learnings that are
143	  explicitly machine-local and never shared.
144	
145	What the native stack still does **not** do — the whitespace Claudinite
146	occupies (absence verified across the plugins/marketplaces/settings/memory
147	docs): plugins converge *clients* (a per-user cache outside the repo), not
148	*repos*; nothing runs convention checks in CI; nothing opens PRs against
149	consuming repos to converge committed files with a canon; and no path exists
150	from one developer's local learnings to a reviewed shared canon. Even the
151	client-convergence story is uneven today: centrally-mandated plugins land
152	unattended on the desktop/web apps but not in the CLI, where the same
153	managed-settings config still needs a human running install commands (or a
154	container image baked ahead of time) — Anthropic's own tracker calls this
155	"not planned," not merely unshipped. The risk to watch is pace: scheduled
156	tasks, auto memory, and org plugin sync all shipped within about nine
157	months. That pace is not uniform, though, and the
158	unevenness is itself the signal: across the same window Anthropic shipped
159	three distribution features and did *not* ship cross-vendor interop, despite
160	AGENTS.md support being the loudest request in its own tracker (above).
161	Absorption has been fast on distribution and absent on interop — so the
162	interop-facing whitespace looks more durable than the raw nine-month cadence
163	suggests.
164	
165	## Direct rivals: syncing rules across repos
166	
167	The category is crowded, young (almost everything created May 2025–June
168	2026), fragmented, and almost entirely free OSS. Star counts verified via
169	GitHub API on 2026-07-31:
170	
171	- **intellectronica/ruler** (2,833 ★, active) — "Centralise Your AI Coding
172	  Assistant Instructions"; a `.ruler/` directory concatenated into 30+
173	  agent-specific files. Single-repo only. Its README does ship a CI example
174	  that fails on uncommitted generated-file diffs — file-drift checking, the
175	  category's strongest "enforcement."
176	- **dyoshikawa/rulesync** (1,273 ★, 298 npm releases, very active) — CLI
177	  generating configs for 30+ tools from one `.rulesync/` source. Its
178	  supported-tools matrix now lists "checks" and "hooks" as feature columns —
179	  category vocabulary drifting toward checks without shipping enforcement.
180	- **RuleSync (rulesync.dev)** — the only commercial player found: a hosted
181	  dashboard + `rsc pull/push` CLI syncing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules
182	  across repos, with a CI-failable `check` command. Free during beta, team
183	  plans "planned." Ranks #1 for the literal query "sync CLAUDE.md across
184	  repos." Unrelated to the dyoshikawa CLI despite the name.
185	- **Goldziher/ai-rulez** (135 ★) — the rival with the strongest enforcement
186	  language: pre-commit hooks literally named `ai-rulez-enforce`, a
187	  `verify` command, and cross-repo "remote includes." All of it targets
188	  config-file integrity, not the code the agent writes.
189	- **agent-sh/agnix** (372 ★, Rust) — a 444-rule *linter for agent config
190	  files* (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hooks, MCP) with a CI GitHub
191	  Action. No sync; complementary evidence for the checks-on-config trend.
192	- **yujiosaka/knowhub** (41 ★) — dormant: last push 2025-07-24, two npm
193	  releases ever. The earlier open question about its enforcement is answered:
194	  file-sync verification only.
195	- **lbb00/ai-rules-sync** (35 ★) — cross-repo team sharing via symlinked
196	  central git repos, 12+ tools; npm activity stalled March 2026. No
197	  enforcement.
198	- **fabian-barney/ai-rules** (3 ★) — a content repo vendored via git subtree
199	  pinned to tagged releases; prior art for the vendored-versioned-unit idea,
200	  no tooling.
201	- **Sync AI Agent Rules** (GitHub Action, 1 ★) — compiles layered rules from
202	  a central repo and auto-commits them into agent files; pushes updates,
203	  gates nothing.
204	- **ranyitz/aicm** (36 ★) — closest architectural precedent to packs:
205	  installable npm packages bundling rules/commands/skills/hooks
206	  (`@company/ai-preset`), but outputs are regenerated into gitignored dirs,
207	  and no enforcement or convergence.
208	- Fragmentation is extreme: at least ten distinct repos named "agentsync"
209	  were created Dec 2025–Jun 2026, all under 60 stars — nobody owns the niche.
210	  Re-checked 2026-08-02: the most active of them, **dallay/agentsync** (52 ★,
211	  Rust, last push 2026-08-01), synchronises agent configs across assistants
212	  via *symbolic links* — the newest live entrant in the category is still
213	  file-placement machinery with no auto-PR and no CI gate.
214	
215	Category-level answers to this page's former open questions:
216	
217	- **Enforcement**: yes-but-narrowly. Five tools advertise CI-failable checks
218	  (ruler, ai-rulez, agnix, rulesync.dev, spxrogers/agentsync), every one
219	  scoped to config-file drift or config-file lint. None runs checks on the
220	  work product, blocks an agent session, or opens convergence PRs. The
221	  sharpened differentiation line: *they check that the rules arrived;
222	  Claudinite checks that the rules are followed.*
223	- **Business models**: except hosted RuleSync, every surveyed tool (15+) is
224	  unmonetized MIT/Apache/Unlicense OSS — an opening, and a price-anchor risk.
225	- **Marketing**: every headline is a movement verb (synchronize / centralise /
226	  share / find); multi-agent breadth (30+/31/20/12+ tools) is the default
227	  marketing axis, making Claudinite's Claude-Code-only focus unusual in the
228	  field. No rival names enforcement in its headline.
229	
230	## Adjacent gravity wells
231	
232	- **Vercel's `npx skills` ecosystem** — vercel-labs/skills (27,660 ★) and
233	  vercel-labs/agent-skills (29,638 ★) in about six months: a "package manager
234	  for AI coding agents" across 17+ agents, with the skills.sh directory.
235	  Distribution only — no checks, no CI, no convergence — but it validates
236	  versioned vendored agent-knowledge packages at two orders of magnitude more
237	  adoption than any rule-sync tool.
238	- **Curated content lists**: hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code (51,368 ★)
239	  overtook the 8-months-older PatrickJS/awesome-cursorrules (40,476 ★) —
240	  convention-sharing energy has moved to Claude Code. Fork counts (3.4k/4.4k)
241	  indicate copy-into-my-project behavior with no update path.
242	- **steipete/agent-rules** (5,702 ★), the category's most-starred rules
243	  content repo, is archived — static rules-content repos are being
244	  superseded, plausibly by the skills ecosystem.
245	- **cursor.directory** monetizes free rules browsing indirectly (~$35k/mo via
246	  jobs/ads per its founder's public claims) — attention, not governance.
247	- **davila7/claude-code-templates** (30,020 ★, aitmpl.com) is the largest
248	  community hub for Claude Code assets, independent of Anthropic's plugin
249	  system.
250	
251	## From above: enterprise scorecard vendors
252	
253	Internal-developer-portal vendors sell "standards enforced across many
254	repos" to enterprises as **scorecards** (checks graded across a service
255	fleet, with levels and campaign deadlines), and in 2025–2026 every one of
256	them pivoted to AI-agent governance:
257	
258	- **Cortex** rebranded "mission control for the AI software factory" and
259	  ships AI-governance scorecards that check "which repositories have proper
260	  AI instructions" — observation of config presence, not authoring or
261	  convergence. It published Claudinite's exact thesis as marketing: "AI is
262	  writing your code. Who's watching your standards?" (Sept 2025).
263	- **Port** repositioned as an "Agentic SDLC" platform that auto-discovers
264	  "agents, MCPs, skills so you can enforce your standards."
265	- **OpsLevel** markets a portal that "enforces standards automatically" and
266	  spun out **Tidra AI** — the one IDP product found that *remediates* with
267	  auto-PRs across every repo in scope (campaign-driven, not a continuous
268	  convergence-to-canon loop).
269	- **Spotify Soundcheck** (paid Backstage plugin) shipped MCP actions so
270	  Claude Code and Cursor can *query* failing checks — scorecards made
271	  readable by agents, the inverse of governing what agents follow.
272	- The category norm remains observe-and-nudge (notifications, Jira tickets,
273	  deadlines); default-on auto-PR convergence stays ahead of it.
274	
275	Deeper enterprise-buyer analysis (procurement gates, ranked requirements)
276	lives in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md).
277	
278	## Sources
279	
280	- [Linux Foundation announces the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/linux-foundation-announces-the-formation-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation-aaif-anchored-by-new-project-contributions-including-model-context-protocol-mcp-goose-and-agentsmd-302636897.html) — AGENTS.md donation, 60,000+ projects, members

# Market

The competitive landscape for Claudinite: the open substrate standards every
coding-agent user already has on disk, the platform-native layer Anthropic now
ships itself, the direct rule-sync competitors, the adjacent content
ecosystems, and the enterprise vendors encroaching from above. Business models
and price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); customer
segments in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md); what this means for
Claudinite in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).

## Key insights

- Anthropic ships the session half natively, but CLI auto-install of org-mandated plugins was closed "not planned."
- Nobody converges repos: no auto-PR loop from a canon, no CI convention gates; native auto memory is machine-local, never shared.
- Rival enforcement is config-drift only: they check the rules arrived; nothing checks the rules are followed.
- The rule-sync category is nearly all free OSS under 3k stars; the one hosted SaaS (rulesync.dev) is in free beta.
- Enterprise scorecard vendors (Cortex, Port, OpsLevel) now sell AI-agent governance from above; OpsLevel's Tidra ships auto-PRs.
- Anthropic's own docs say CLAUDE.md is "context, not enforced configuration" — the vendor states Claudinite's premise.
- The AGENTS.md request (4,944 👍) was closed *completed* on 2026-08-17 by shipping an import; Claude Code still won't read the file.

## The substrate: per-repo convention files

Every agent-facing repo already carries at least one plain-text convention
file, and Claudinite has to interoperate with all of them rather than compete
with them:

- **AGENTS.md** is the vendor-neutral standard: a plain-markdown,
  no-frontmatter file at the repo root, formalized as an open spec in August
  2025 and donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) on
  December 9, 2025 — alongside MCP and Block's goose, with AWS, Anthropic,
  Google, Microsoft and OpenAI as platinum members — citing adoption by more
  than 60,000 open-source projects.
  *Correction (2026-07-31):* this page previously said "read by 30+ agents,"
  citing the codersera guide; that page actually says "native support in 20+
  tools," and the "30+" figure appears to have been conflated with Ruler's
  own supported-agent marketing. The scale citation is now the LF
  announcement (primary).
- The spec itself is deliberately minimal — "a README for agents," no
  required fields, no schema — and says nothing about enforcement, machine
  checks, versioning, or packaged conventions. The only shared semantics are
  precedence (nearest file wins; chat instructions override). Enforcement and
  packaging are out of scope, i.e. open territory.
- **CLAUDE.md** is Claude Code's project-memory file, now a four-level
  hierarchy (managed policy / user / project / local) plus path-scoped
  `.claude/rules/` files and `@path` imports. Claude Code still reads
  CLAUDE.md natively, not AGENTS.md — the docs recommend an `@AGENTS.md`
  import or symlink as the bridge. Community best practice still converges on
  keeping it under ~200 lines (spot-checked 2026-07-31: the cited guide is
  alive and still says this).
- **The AGENTS.md request was closed as completed on 2026-08-17 — and Claude
  Code still does not read the file** (researched 2026-08-21).
  `anthropics/claude-code` #6235 "Feature Request: Support AGENTS.md." was
  closed `completed` by the Claude Code lead (bcherny) at 2026-08-17T03:37Z,
  after twelve months and 4,944 👍 (6,367 total reactions, 374 comments) —
  the largest quantified demand signal in the agent-config space, and now
  answered by an *import*, not by native reading. The memory doc, re-fetched
  the same day the issue's last update landed, still says flatly "Claude Code
  reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`"; what shipped is `/import` (Claude Code
  v2.1.213+), which "appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as
  `AGENTS.md` to the matching `CLAUDE.md`", alongside `/init` under
  `CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1` reading AGENTS.md at generation time. Both are
  one-time copies into CLAUDE.md — the same bridge this wiki has recorded
  since 2026-08-02, now blessed as the official answer. The read gap is
  therefore *durable by decision*, not by backlog: the interop whitespace
  stays open, and a copy-in bridge is itself a drift source, which is the
  territory Claudinite is already in.
- **Anthropic now states the enforcement gap in its own docs, in Claudinite's
  own terms** (primary page, 2026-08-21). The memory doc's opening comparison
  says of CLAUDE.md and auto memory: "Claude treats them as context, not
  enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude
  decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead," and its managed-policy section
  draws the same line: "Settings rules are enforced by the client regardless
  of what Claude decides to do. CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's
  behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer." The same page tells teams
  to "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file" because "longer files
  consume more context and reduce adherence." The platform vendor is the
  primary source for the premise the whole rule-sync category is built on
  top of and never addresses.
- **Auto memory is the native learning loop — and it is machine-local by
  design.** Claude Code writes its own notes from a user's corrections into
  `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`, on by default. The doc is explicit
  that "Auto memory is machine-local... Files are not shared across machines
  or cloud environments" (primary page, 2026-08-21), and only the first 200
  lines / 25KB of its index load per session. Nothing native promotes a
  lesson from one machine to a team, a repo, or a fleet.
- **SKILL.md / Agent Skills** became a cross-vendor open standard: Anthropic
  published the spec (agentskills.io, Dec 2025), and by mid-2026 roughly 40
  tools — OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, JetBrains
  Junie, Block's goose — read the same format. anthropics/skills sits at
  ~165.3k stars (verified via GitHub API 2026-07-31). The spec mandates only
  `name`/`description` frontmatter; nothing about checks or distribution.
- **Cursor** keeps its `.cursor/rules/` directory; Cursor Teams now also
  markets "Team Commands" with a team baseline and drift detection — the
  platform vendor absorbing single-tool rule sharing natively.
- **GitHub Copilot** keeps `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and reads
  AGENTS.md; GitHub's own blog mined 2,500+ AGENTS.md files for guidance.

None of these substrate formats answer the question Claudinite is for: how
the *same* convention, once refined, reaches every repo that shares it,
stays current there, and is *checked* rather than trusted.

## The platform layer: what Claude Code now ships natively

The largest competitive change since this page was seeded is Anthropic's own
distribution stack (all verified against current Claude Code docs,
2026-07-31):

- **Plugins** (announced October 9, 2025) bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP
  servers, LSP servers, and default settings into versioned packages,
  distributed through decentralized **marketplaces** (`marketplace.json` in
  any git repo/npm source, semver or SHA pinning, background auto-update).
- **Plugins can be centrally mandated — but not uniformly across surfaces.**
  Project-level `extraKnownMarketplaces`/`enabledPlugins`, managed-settings
  force-enable, `strictKnownMarketplaces` lockdown, container seed dirs, and
  claude.ai org-level plugin sync on Team/Enterprise plans (per-plugin
  installation preferences — Installed by default / Available for install /
  Required / Not available) all exist as mechanisms.
  *Correction (2026-08-09):* this page previously left the impression the
  CLI itself honors `enabledPlugins`/`extraKnownMarketplaces` automatically.
  It doesn't. [anthropics/claude-code#45323](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/45323)
  ("CLI: Auto-install plugins from org managed settings") documents that the
  CLI fetches the managed-settings marketplace into
  `~/.claude/remote-settings.json` at startup but never registers it in
  `known_marketplaces.json` or installs the listed plugin — the org's admin
  still has to have every user run `/plugin marketplace add` and
  `/plugin install` by hand, or bake plugins into a container image at build
  time via `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`. Filed April 2026, the issue was
  closed **"not planned."** The same managed settings *do* auto-install on
  the desktop and web apps per the issue's own comparison and the Claude
  Help Center's org-plugin-management article (that page egress-blocked to
  this pass's fetcher — via search-quoted context, not opened directly) — so
  the CLI, Claudinite's own delivery surface, is specifically the one where
  central mandate still isn't unattended.
- **Managed settings** give admins non-overridable org-wide permission rules,
  hooks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), MCP allowlists, model restrictions, and
  even an org-wide CLAUDE.md blob — delivered by MDM, machine-wide.
- **Hooks** provide deterministic in-session blocking (exit code 2 /
  `permissionDecision: "deny"`); Anthropic's own docs route enforcement away
  from prose to hooks — validating Claudinite's thesis while shipping the
  session-side half of it.
- **Native scheduling** arrived in three tiers (session cron//loop, cloud
  Routines, Desktop tasks); **auto memory** is per-project learnings that are
  explicitly machine-local and never shared.

What the native stack still does **not** do — the whitespace Claudinite
occupies (absence verified across the plugins/marketplaces/settings/memory
docs): plugins converge *clients* (a per-user cache outside the repo), not
*repos*; nothing runs convention checks in CI; nothing opens PRs against
consuming repos to converge committed files with a canon; and no path exists
from one developer's local learnings to a reviewed shared canon. Even the
client-convergence story is uneven today: centrally-mandated plugins land
unattended on the desktop/web apps but not in the CLI, where the same
managed-settings config still needs a human running install commands (or a
container image baked ahead of time) — Anthropic's own tracker calls this
"not planned," not merely unshipped. The risk to watch is pace: scheduled
tasks, auto memory, and org plugin sync all shipped within about nine
months. That pace is not uniform, though, and the
unevenness is itself the signal: across the same window Anthropic shipped
three distribution features and did *not* ship cross-vendor interop, despite
AGENTS.md support being the loudest request in its own tracker (above).
Absorption has been fast on distribution and absent on interop — so the
interop-facing whitespace looks more durable than the raw nine-month cadence
suggests.

## Direct rivals: syncing rules across repos

The category is crowded, young (almost everything created May 2025–June
2026), fragmented, and almost entirely free OSS. Star counts verified via
GitHub API on 2026-07-31:

- **intellectronica/ruler** (2,833 ★, active) — "Centralise Your AI Coding
  Assistant Instructions"; a `.ruler/` directory concatenated into 30+
  agent-specific files. Single-repo only. Its README does ship a CI example
  that fails on uncommitted generated-file diffs — file-drift checking, the
  category's strongest "enforcement."
- **dyoshikawa/rulesync** (1,273 ★, 298 npm releases, very active) — CLI
  generating configs for 30+ tools from one `.rulesync/` source. Its
  supported-tools matrix now lists "checks" and "hooks" as feature columns —
  category vocabulary drifting toward checks without shipping enforcement.
- **RuleSync (rulesync.dev)** — the only commercial player found: a hosted
  dashboard + `rsc pull/push` CLI syncing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules
  across repos, with a CI-failable `check` command. Free during beta, team
  plans "planned." Ranks #1 for the literal query "sync CLAUDE.md across
  repos." Unrelated to the dyoshikawa CLI despite the name.
- **Goldziher/ai-rulez** (135 ★) — the rival with the strongest enforcement
  language: pre-commit hooks literally named `ai-rulez-enforce`, a
  `verify` command, and cross-repo "remote includes." All of it targets
  config-file integrity, not the code the agent writes.
- **agent-sh/agnix** (372 ★, Rust) — a 444-rule *linter for agent config
  files* (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hooks, MCP) with a CI GitHub
  Action. No sync; complementary evidence for the checks-on-config trend.
- **yujiosaka/knowhub** (41 ★) — dormant: last push 2025-07-24, two npm
  releases ever. The earlier open question about its enforcement is answered:
  file-sync verification only.
- **lbb00/ai-rules-sync** (35 ★) — cross-repo team sharing via symlinked
  central git repos, 12+ tools; npm activity stalled March 2026. No
  enforcement.
- **fabian-barney/ai-rules** (3 ★) — a content repo vendored via git subtree
  pinned to tagged releases; prior art for the vendored-versioned-unit idea,
  no tooling.
- **Sync AI Agent Rules** (GitHub Action, 1 ★) — compiles layered rules from
  a central repo and auto-commits them into agent files; pushes updates,
  gates nothing.
- **ranyitz/aicm** (36 ★) — closest architectural precedent to packs:
  installable npm packages bundling rules/commands/skills/hooks
  (`@company/ai-preset`), but outputs are regenerated into gitignored dirs,
  and no enforcement or convergence.
- Fragmentation is extreme: at least ten distinct repos named "agentsync"
  were created Dec 2025–Jun 2026, all under 60 stars — nobody owns the niche.
  Re-checked 2026-08-02: the most active of them, **dallay/agentsync** (52 ★,
  Rust, last push 2026-08-01), synchronises agent configs across assistants
  via *symbolic links* — the newest live entrant in the category is still
  file-placement machinery with no auto-PR and no CI gate.

Category-level answers to this page's former open questions:

- **Enforcement**: yes-but-narrowly. Five tools advertise CI-failable checks
  (ruler, ai-rulez, agnix, rulesync.dev, spxrogers/agentsync), every one
  scoped to config-file drift or config-file lint. None runs checks on the
  work product, blocks an agent session, or opens convergence PRs. The
  sharpened differentiation line: *they check that the rules arrived;
  Claudinite checks that the rules are followed.*
- **Business models**: except hosted RuleSync, every surveyed tool (15+) is
  unmonetized MIT/Apache/Unlicense OSS — an opening, and a price-anchor risk.
- **Marketing**: every headline is a movement verb (synchronize / centralise /
  share / find); multi-agent breadth (30+/31/20/12+ tools) is the default
  marketing axis, making Claudinite's Claude-Code-only focus unusual in the
  field. No rival names enforcement in its headline.

## Adjacent gravity wells

- **Vercel's `npx skills` ecosystem** — vercel-labs/skills (27,660 ★) and
  vercel-labs/agent-skills (29,638 ★) in about six months: a "package manager
  for AI coding agents" across 17+ agents, with the skills.sh directory.
  Distribution only — no checks, no CI, no convergence — but it validates
  versioned vendored agent-knowledge packages at two orders of magnitude more
  adoption than any rule-sync tool.
- **Curated content lists**: hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code (51,368 ★)
  overtook the 8-months-older PatrickJS/awesome-cursorrules (40,476 ★) —
  convention-sharing energy has moved to Claude Code. Fork counts (3.4k/4.4k)
  indicate copy-into-my-project behavior with no update path.
- **steipete/agent-rules** (5,702 ★), the category's most-starred rules
  content repo, is archived — static rules-content repos are being
  superseded, plausibly by the skills ecosystem.
- **cursor.directory** monetizes free rules browsing indirectly (~$35k/mo via
  jobs/ads per its founder's public claims) — attention, not governance.
- **davila7/claude-code-templates** (30,020 ★, aitmpl.com) is the largest
  community hub for Claude Code assets, independent of Anthropic's plugin
  system.

## From above: enterprise scorecard vendors

Internal-developer-portal vendors sell "standards enforced across many
repos" to enterprises as **scorecards** (checks graded across a service
fleet, with levels and campaign deadlines), and in 2025–2026 every one of
them pivoted to AI-agent governance:

- **Cortex** rebranded "mission control for the AI software factory" and
  ships AI-governance scorecards that check "which repositories have proper
  AI instructions" — observation of config presence, not authoring or
  convergence. It published Claudinite's exact thesis as marketing: "AI is
  writing your code. Who's watching your standards?" (Sept 2025).
- **Port** repositioned as an "Agentic SDLC" platform that auto-discovers
  "agents, MCPs, skills so you can enforce your standards."
- **OpsLevel** markets a portal that "enforces standards automatically" and
  spun out **Tidra AI** — the one IDP product found that *remediates* with
  auto-PRs across every repo in scope (campaign-driven, not a continuous
  convergence-to-canon loop).
- **Spotify Soundcheck** (paid Backstage plugin) shipped MCP actions so
  Claude Code and Cursor can *query* failing checks — scorecards made
  readable by agents, the inverse of governing what agents follow.
- The category norm remains observe-and-nudge (notifications, Jira tickets,
  deadlines); default-on auto-PR convergence stays ahead of it.

Deeper enterprise-buyer analysis (procurement gates, ranked requirements)
lives in [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md).

## Open questions

- What does dyoshikawa/rulesync's "checks" feature column actually generate
  (its docs site was egress-blocked this pass), and does it map to native
  check primitives in Amp/Cursor?
- rulesync.dev's concrete paid pricing and team once out of beta — the first
  direct commercial test of this category's willingness to pay.
- npm weekly downloads for ruler/rulesync/knowhub/ai-rules-sync (npm stats
  endpoints were egress-blocked; adoption is star/release-cadence-based).
- Confirm directly (not via search-quoted context — support.claude.com is
  still egress-blocked to this pass's fetcher) that claude.ai desktop/web org
  plugin sync actually auto-installs today; the CLI half of the question is
  now settled (it doesn't — anthropics/claude-code#45323, closed "not
  planned"), but the desktop/web side still rests on secondary
  characterization.
- Is `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`-at-build-time Anthropic's intended
  permanent answer for CLI fleets, or does #45323 being closed "not planned"
  just mean deprioritized rather than rejected in principle? No roadmap
  signal found this pass.
- Answered 2026-08-21: it was the "the import is the answer" stance —
  #6235 closed `completed` on the `/import` command, with the docs unchanged
  on native reading. Still open: is that final, or a staging post? No
  maintainer statement was located this pass beyond the close itself.
- Do the rival CLIs treat Claude Code's `@AGENTS.md` import/symlink bridge as
  a first-class output target? If the bridge is becoming the de-facto
  standard, emitting it is cheaper than emitting a second rules corpus.
- Current plugin counts in `claude-plugins-official`/`community` and their
  growth rate — the pace of native absorption is the platform-risk metric.
- Does any AAIF working group plan to add structure (schemas, checks,
  versioning) to AGENTS.md? No evidence found this pass; re-check.
- Whether Cursor Teams' drift-detecting Team Commands extend beyond
  Cursor-native rules (to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) — if so, first-party
  absorption reaches further than assumed.
- Has any tool announced a Renovate-style auto-PR convergence bot for agent
  conventions? Re-checked 2026-08-02 (web search plus a GitHub repository
  search restricted to tools pushed since June 2026): none found — every
  live entrant is a CLI, a generator, or a symlinker. Absence of evidence
  from two search surfaces, not proof; re-check next pass.

  closed `completed` 2026-08-17 while the memory doc still says Claude Code

1	# Business
2	
3	Business models and price anchors for Claudinite: what adjacent devtools
4	charge, which commercial archetypes survive contact with a "plain vendored
5	files, no server" product, and what is genuinely scarce enough to price.
6	Method lessons live in [`Methods/`](../Methods/README.md); who would pay in
7	[`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md). Nothing on this page is a decision —
8	the human-reviewed distillation is
9	[`product-requirements/`](../product-requirements/README.md).
10	
11	## Key insights
12	
13	- Vendored files are trivially copyable — the sellable scarcities are the convergence bot, canon updates, private packs, and SLA.
14	- Governance tooling prices at $19–29/seat/mo (Copilot Business, GitLab Premium); AI-multiplier tools reach $60–200.
15	- pre-commit.ci's $0-for-OSS / $10–100/mo flat org tiers is the closest live pricing precedent for a config-bot product.
16	- Only GitHub Apps can be paid Marketplace listings (95% to publisher) — Actions and plain files cannot.
17	- Spotify sells its paid Backstage plugins only via negotiated AWS private offers — self-serve paid content looked weak.
18	- Sponsorware is hobby-scale: GitHub Sponsors totals ~$100M cumulative over ~7 years across ~70k maintainers.
19	- Behavioral seats (Snyk: committed in 90 days; CodeRabbit: opened a PR) are the emerging norm for repo-attached tools.
20	
21	## Price anchors (mid-2026)
22	
23	Caveat on provenance: several vendor pricing pages 403-block fetchers; where
24	a price rests on vendor-domain search quotes rather than a directly-opened
25	page, the source bullet says so.
26	
27	**AI assistant/agent seats** (what the target user already pays):
28	
29	- GitHub Copilot: Free / Pro $10 / Pro+ $39 / Max $100 per user/mo
30	  (vendor page, opened directly); Business $19, Enterprise $39 per user/mo
31	  (GitHub docs).
32	- Cursor: Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200; team seats $32 (Standard) and $96
33	  (Premium) per seat/mo annual, after the June 2026 teams-pricing change
34	  (vendor pages via search quotes).
35	- Claude: Pro $20, Max $100–200; Team Standard $25/seat (5-seat min), Team
36	  Premium $100/seat annual — Claude Code rides Premium seats; Enterprise
37	  custom (triangulated secondary sources; vendor page blocked).
38	
39	**Repo-attached quality/governance tooling** (the band Claudinite would be
40	judged in):
41	
42	- Codecov Team $5 / Pro $12 per user/mo; Snyk Team $25 per contributing
43	  dev/mo (caps at 10 licenses before forced sales contact).
44	- CodeRabbit Lite $12 / Pro $24 / Pro Plus $48 per dev/mo annual — billing
45	  only devs who open PRs.
46	- SonarQube Cloud prices the *codebase*, not the humans: from $32/mo per
47	  100k LOC — the notable per-repo-style metric.
48	- pre-commit.ci: $0 open source, $10/mo personal private, $20/mo org ≤25
49	  users, $100/mo org ≤100 users (Marketplace listing, opened directly).
50	- Atlassian Compass was the scorecard category's floor at $0/$8/$25 per
51	  user/mo — now being sunset into DX (see Customers wiki for the
52	  consolidation signal).
53	- Enterprise scorecard platforms (transaction data, not list prices):
54	  OpsLevel ~$400–700/dev/yr; Cortex enterprise contracts $100k–250k+/yr;
55	  Port free ≤15 seats then quote-gated with SSO/RBAC/audit behind Enterprise.
56	- GitLab open-core: Free / Premium $29 / Ultimate ~$99 per user/mo, Duo AI
57	  add-on +$19 — the paid line drawn at org-level controls, not core function.
58	- npm private packages: $7/user/mo — the canonical private-registry price.
59	
60	## Archetypes that survive "plain files, no server"
61	
62	Each with its named precedent and the implication for Claudinite:
63	
64	- **Hosted-service-on-OSS** (pre-commit.ci, Renovate/Mend): the files and
65	  mechanism are free; the *bot that runs the loop for you* is the product.
66	  Claudinite's equivalent sellable: operating the nightly
67	  baselining/convergence fleet and the scheduled agentic maintenance. The
68	  strongest-fit archetype — it prices exactly what is ongoing.
69	- **Open-core / enterprise edition** (GitLab, Mend Renovate EE): core free,
70	  paid tier at org-level controls — scale, reporting, compliance, SLA. Maps
71	  to fleet reporting, private canon, multi-team controls.
72	- **Private-registry pattern** (npm, Docker Hub): public packs free, private
73	  packs paid (~$7–24/user/mo band). Maps directly to "your org's private
74	  canon and packs."
75	- **Support/SLA subscription** (Tidelift): validated as strategic value but
76	  acquired (Sonar, Dec 2024) rather than scaled standalone — treat as a
77	  deal-sweetener, not the model.
78	- **Paid content on a free platform** (Spotify's Backstage plugin bundle):
79	  exists, but Spotify retreated from public self-serve pricing to AWS
80	  Marketplace private offers — read as weak self-serve demand for paid
81	  plugins; enterprise-negotiated deals instead. A warning against "sell the
82	  packs themselves."
83	- **Marketplace billing** (GitHub): publishers keep 95%, but only GitHub
84	  *Apps* can be paid listings — Actions and files cannot. Marketplace
85	  distribution/billing would require wrapping Claudinite's loop in a GitHub
86	  App, which pushes toward the hosted-bot model anyway.
87	- **Sponsorware**: ceiling too low to matter commercially — ~$100M
88	  *cumulative* across ~70k maintainers in ~7 years; mid-tier maintainers
89	  $500–5k/mo.
90	
91	One-time content sales have no working precedent in this space at product
92	scale — though the indie segment does pay $199–249 one-time for
93	boilerplates (see [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md)), which suggests a
94	one-time *entry* SKU is viable even if recurring revenue must come from the
95	loop.
96	
97	## What the anchors suggest
98	
99	- Per-seat: $10–40/seat/mo is defensible for governance-positioned tooling
100	  (between Codecov's $5 and Copilot Enterprise's $39); the $60–200 AI-premium
101	  band applies only if positioned as a capability multiplier, not
102	  governance.
103	- Flat org tiers: pre-commit.ci's $20/mo (≤25 users) and $100/mo (≤100
104	  users) is the credible low-end floor; per-repo or per-LOC metrics
105	  (SonarQube-style) are the alternative if seats fit badly.
106	- Seat definition: behavioral ("developers whose repos consume a pack" /
107	  "opened a PR in a governed repo") mitigates the uneven-adoption objection,
108	  per Snyk and CodeRabbit precedent.
109	- The free tier is load-bearing in every surviving precedent: free for
110	  public/OSS repos is how pre-commit.ci, Renovate, Codecov and CodeRabbit
111	  all built their funnels.

# Business

Business models and price anchors for Claudinite: what adjacent devtools
charge, which commercial archetypes survive contact with a "plain vendored
files, no server" product, and what is genuinely scarce enough to price.
Method lessons live in [`Methods/`](../Methods/README.md); who would pay in
[`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md). Nothing on this page is a decision —
the human-reviewed distillation is
[`product-requirements/`](../product-requirements/README.md).

## Key insights

- Vendored files are trivially copyable — the sellable scarcities are the convergence bot, canon updates, private packs, and SLA.
- Governance tooling prices at $19–29/seat/mo (Copilot Business, GitLab Premium); AI-multiplier tools reach $60–200.
- pre-commit.ci's $0-for-OSS / $10–100/mo flat org tiers is the closest live pricing precedent for a config-bot product.
- Only GitHub Apps can be paid Marketplace listings (95% to publisher) — Actions and plain files cannot.
- Spotify sells its paid Backstage plugins only via negotiated AWS private offers — self-serve paid content looked weak.
- Sponsorware is hobby-scale: GitHub Sponsors totals ~$100M cumulative over ~7 years across ~70k maintainers.
- Behavioral seats (Snyk: committed in 90 days; CodeRabbit: opened a PR) are the emerging norm for repo-attached tools.

## Price anchors (mid-2026)

Caveat on provenance: several vendor pricing pages 403-block fetchers; where
a price rests on vendor-domain search quotes rather than a directly-opened
page, the source bullet says so.

**AI assistant/agent seats** (what the target user already pays):

- GitHub Copilot: Free / Pro $10 / Pro+ $39 / Max $100 per user/mo
  (vendor page, opened directly); Business $19, Enterprise $39 per user/mo
  (GitHub docs).
- Cursor: Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200; team seats $32 (Standard) and $96
  (Premium) per seat/mo annual, after the June 2026 teams-pricing change
  (vendor pages via search quotes).
- Claude: Pro $20, Max $100–200; Team Standard $25/seat (5-seat min), Team
  Premium $100/seat annual — Claude Code rides Premium seats; Enterprise
  custom (triangulated secondary sources; vendor page blocked).

**Repo-attached quality/governance tooling** (the band Claudinite would be
judged in):

- Codecov Team $5 / Pro $12 per user/mo; Snyk Team $25 per contributing
  dev/mo (caps at 10 licenses before forced sales contact).
- CodeRabbit Lite $12 / Pro $24 / Pro Plus $48 per dev/mo annual — billing
  only devs who open PRs.
- SonarQube Cloud prices the *codebase*, not the humans: from $32/mo per
  100k LOC — the notable per-repo-style metric.
- pre-commit.ci: $0 open source, $10/mo personal private, $20/mo org ≤25
  users, $100/mo org ≤100 users (Marketplace listing, opened directly).
- Atlassian Compass was the scorecard category's floor at $0/$8/$25 per
  user/mo — now being sunset into DX (see Customers wiki for the
  consolidation signal).
- Enterprise scorecard platforms (transaction data, not list prices):
  OpsLevel ~$400–700/dev/yr; Cortex enterprise contracts $100k–250k+/yr;
  Port free ≤15 seats then quote-gated with SSO/RBAC/audit behind Enterprise.
- GitLab open-core: Free / Premium $29 / Ultimate ~$99 per user/mo, Duo AI
  add-on +$19 — the paid line drawn at org-level controls, not core function.
- npm private packages: $7/user/mo — the canonical private-registry price.

## Archetypes that survive "plain files, no server"

Each with its named precedent and the implication for Claudinite:

- **Hosted-service-on-OSS** (pre-commit.ci, Renovate/Mend): the files and
  mechanism are free; the *bot that runs the loop for you* is the product.
  Claudinite's equivalent sellable: operating the nightly
  baselining/convergence fleet and the scheduled agentic maintenance. The
  strongest-fit archetype — it prices exactly what is ongoing.
- **Open-core / enterprise edition** (GitLab, Mend Renovate EE): core free,
  paid tier at org-level controls — scale, reporting, compliance, SLA. Maps
  to fleet reporting, private canon, multi-team controls.
- **Private-registry pattern** (npm, Docker Hub): public packs free, private
  packs paid (~$7–24/user/mo band). Maps directly to "your org's private
  canon and packs."
- **Support/SLA subscription** (Tidelift): validated as strategic value but
  acquired (Sonar, Dec 2024) rather than scaled standalone — treat as a
  deal-sweetener, not the model.
- **Paid content on a free platform** (Spotify's Backstage plugin bundle):
  exists, but Spotify retreated from public self-serve pricing to AWS
  Marketplace private offers — read as weak self-serve demand for paid
  plugins; enterprise-negotiated deals instead. A warning against "sell the
  packs themselves."
- **Marketplace billing** (GitHub): publishers keep 95%, but only GitHub
  *Apps* can be paid listings — Actions and files cannot. Marketplace
  distribution/billing would require wrapping Claudinite's loop in a GitHub
  App, which pushes toward the hosted-bot model anyway.
- **Sponsorware**: ceiling too low to matter commercially — ~$100M
  *cumulative* across ~70k maintainers in ~7 years; mid-tier maintainers
  $500–5k/mo.

One-time content sales have no working precedent in this space at product
scale — though the indie segment does pay $199–249 one-time for
boilerplates (see [`Customers/`](../Customers/README.md)), which suggests a
one-time *entry* SKU is viable even if recurring revenue must come from the
loop.

## What the anchors suggest

- Per-seat: $10–40/seat/mo is defensible for governance-positioned tooling
  (between Codecov's $5 and Copilot Enterprise's $39); the $60–200 AI-premium
  band applies only if positioned as a capability multiplier, not
  governance.
- Flat org tiers: pre-commit.ci's $20/mo (≤25 users) and $100/mo (≤100
  users) is the credible low-end floor; per-repo or per-LOC metrics
  (SonarQube-style) are the alternative if seats fit badly.
- Seat definition: behavioral ("developers whose repos consume a pack" /
  "opened a PR in a governed repo") mitigates the uneven-adoption objection,
  per Snyk and CodeRabbit precedent.
- The free tier is load-bearing in every surviving precedent: free for
  public/OSS repos is how pre-commit.ci, Renovate, Codecov and CodeRabbit
  all built their funnels.

## Sources

- [GitHub Copilot plans](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans) — individual tiers (opened directly)
- [Copilot org billing — GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/copilot/concepts/billing/organizations-and-enterprises) — Business/Enterprise seats
- [Cursor teams pricing change](https://cursor.com/blog/teams-pricing-june-2026) and [teams pricing docs](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/pricing) — via search quotes (site 403s fetchers)
- [Claude Team pricing 2026 — tygartmedia](https://tygartmedia.com/claude-team-pricing-2026-standard-premium-seats/), corroborated by [aipricing.guru](https://www.aipricing.guru/subscriptions/claude-team-premium/) and [intuitionlabs](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/claude-pricing-plans-api-costs) — secondary triangulation
- [pre-commit ci — GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/pre-commit-ci) — tiers (opened directly)
- [Sonar plans & pricing](https://www.sonarsource.com/plans-and-pricing/) — per-LOC entry tier (via search quotes)
- [Codecov pricing](https://about.codecov.io/pricing/), [Snyk plans](https://snyk.io/plans/), [CodeRabbit plans](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/management/plans) — via search quotes
- [Compass pricing — Atlassian](https://www.atlassian.com/software/compass/pricing)
- [OpsLevel pricing — Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/opslevel), [Cortex — Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/cortex), [Port cost framework](https://platformengineeringcost.com/port-cost) — transaction-data estimates
- [GitLab pricing 2026 — costbench](https://costbench.com/software/developer-tools/gitlab/) (vendor page blocked), corroborated by [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/gitlab)
- [npm products](https://www.npmjs.com/products) — $7/user private packages
- [Mend Renovate](https://www.mend.io/renovate/) — free bot, paid EE
- [Receiving payment — GitHub Marketplace docs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/github-marketplace/selling-your-app-on-github-marketplace/receiving-payment-for-app-purchases) and [about Marketplace for apps](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/github-marketplace/github-marketplace-overview/about-github-marketplace-for-apps) — 95%/5%, Apps-only
- [Spotify Plugins for Backstage bundle](https://backstage.spotify.com/partners/spotify/bundle/spotify-plugins-bundle/) and [AWS Marketplace listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-ae67cydhcqpei)
- [Sonar acquires Tidelift](https://www.sonarsource.com/company/press-releases/sonar-to-acquire-tidelift/)
- [GitHub Sponsors crosses $100M — Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/21/open-source-github-sponsors-100-million/) and [About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/en/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors)

## Open questions

- Direct confirmation of Cursor/Claude/Snyk/Codecov/Sonar prices on their own
  pricing pages (all 403'd this pass; figures rest on vendor-domain search
  quotes and consistent secondaries).
- Mend Renovate Enterprise's real price (contact-sales; the $250/dev/yr
  figure is third-party) — the closest comparable for a paid convergence
  fleet.
- rulesync.dev's paid team pricing once out of beta — the first direct
  willingness-to-pay signal inside the rule-sync category itself.
- Does pre-commit.ci have an above-100-users tier? None listed — how does
  the flat-tier model extend to enterprise scale?
- Claude Enterprise per-seat price and minimum seats (secondary sources hint
  ~150-user threshold) — bounds what a Claude-Code-attached governance layer
  can plausibly add per seat.
- What did Spotify's plugin bundle actually charge inside private offers?
  Would calibrate the paid-content archetype's real numbers.

## Growth log

- **2026-07-31** — page created in the owner-directed ecosystem research
  pass: price anchors collected across AI-assistant seats, repo-attached
  quality tooling, scorecard platforms and registries; seven commercial
  archetypes assessed against the no-server constraint; scarcity analysis
  (convergence bot / canon stream / private packs / SLA) and indicative
  price bands distilled, all cited with provenance caveats where vendor
  pages were fetch-blocked.

1	# Customers
2	
3	Customer profiles and potential users for Claudinite, in three segments:
4	independent developers, small software shops and agencies (2–50 devs), and
5	large enterprises (100+ engineers, platform teams). For each: who they are,
6	what they do today instead, the trigger moment, and what they would pay.
7	Price anchors live in [`Business/`](../Business/README.md); what this implies
8	for the offering in [`Positioning/`](../Positioning/README.md).
9	
10	## Key insights
11	
12	- 90% of developers use AI at work; only ~24–33% trust its output — the adoption/trust scissor is the buying condition.
13	- Claude Code went from ~3% to 18% work usage in eight months with the category's best satisfaction — the fastest-growing agent.
14	- Users file issues titled "need enforcement mechanism"; the tracker's loudest ask (AGENTS.md, 4,944 👍) closed on an import.
15	- Solo devs run dotfiles and symlinks; agencies copy a shared config repo per client — drift machines with no update path.
16	- Indies pay $199–249 one-time for vendored starter files (ShipFast: $250k in 5 months); shops absorb $125/seat for Claude Premium.
17	- Enterprise near-blockers, in order: security review, multi-agent (AGENTS.md) support, private canon — then metrics and SLA.
18	- Spotify's Fleetshift proved the mechanism at scale: 270k+ fleet PRs, 77% automerged — enterprises already hold this mental model.
19	
20	## The market condition: adoption up, trust down
21	
22	- Stack Overflow 2025 (49k+ respondents): 84% use or plan to use AI tools
23	  (up from 76%), 51% of professionals use them daily — while favorable
24	  sentiment fell to 60% and 46% actively distrust output accuracy; 66% name
25	  "almost right, but not quite" solutions as their top frustration. Only 31%
26	  currently use *agents*; 87% of respondents are concerned about agent
27	  accuracy — Stack Overflow's own framing is "agents on a leash."
28	- DORA 2025 (≈5,000 respondents): 90% of developers use AI at work, 80%+
29	  report productivity gains, yet 30% report little or no trust in
30	  AI-generated code. Its central finding: AI *amplifies* existing
31	  organizational strengths and dysfunctions; quality internal platforms and
32	  a "clear and communicated AI stance" are named mediating capabilities —
33	  and AI adoption still correlates with delivery *instability* where control
34	  systems (testing, version control, feedback loops) haven't kept up.
35	- JetBrains (24,534 devs, 2025): 85% regularly use AI for coding but only
36	  44% call it integrated into their workflow; by its January 2026 pulse, 90%
37	  used at least one AI tool at work.
38	- Claude Code specifically: 18% work usage by January 2026 (24% US/Canada),
39	  up from ~3% mid-2025, with category-best satisfaction (CSAT 91, NPS 54);
40	  Anthropic announced $1B annualized run-rate within ~6 months of GA
41	  (Dec 2025). GitHub Copilot leads usage at 29% but has flatlined.
42	
43	The scissor — near-universal use, low trust, "almost right" output — is the
44	condition a machine-enforced-conventions product sells into: human vigilance
45	does not scale with agent output volume.
46	
47	## Segment: independent developers
48	
49	- **Who**: ~14% of Stack Overflow respondents are freelancers; SlashData
50	  counts 47.2M developers worldwide (36.5M professional) — a ~5M freelance
51	  professional ceiling before filtering to agent users. r/ClaudeAI reached
52	  ~1M members by mid-2026 (+37% in one 90-day window).
53	- **What they do today**: version-control `~/.claude` in a dotfiles repo,
54	  symlink CLAUDE.md/commands/hooks across projects, with explicit gitignore
55	  allowlists; the pattern is common enough that dedicated tools exist
56	  (dot-claude-sync, claude-code-dotfiles). This solves one *machine's*
57	  consistency, not cross-repo drift.
58	- **Documented pain**: multiple anthropics/claude-code issues (verified via
59	  GitHub API 2026-07-31) — #18660 "CLAUDE.md instructions are read but not
60	  reliably followed — need enforcement mechanism", #34132 "Rules in
61	  .claude/rules/ and CLAUDE.md are advisory-only", #32193 "Claude violates
62	  its own mandatory CLAUDE.md instructions"; plus blog posts like "I wrote
63	  200 lines of rules for Claude Code. It ignored them all."
64	- **Trigger moment**: the Nth repo whose CLAUDE.md has drifted from the
65	  others, or the agent visibly violating rules it was given.
66	- **Willingness to pay**: already paying $10–200/mo for the agent itself;
67	  demonstrated $199–249 one-time for vendored starter files (Marc Lou's
68	  ShipFast: $250k in its first 5 months, "own it forever" as the pitch) and
69	  $5–27 for Gumroad rules packs. Realistic band: ~$10–19/mo, or a $29–79
70	  one-time/annual pack license.
71	- **What matters in Claudinite's shape**: plain files (matches how they
72	  already share conventions — the awesome-lists at 51k/40k stars are
73	  copy-paste culture), no account/server, and free-for-public-repos
74	  (every comparable's funnel).
75	
76	## Segment: small shops and agencies (2–50 devs)
77	
78	- **Who**: 57% of employed Stack Overflow respondents work at companies
79	  under 500 employees; Clutch lists 8,500+ US software-development firms (no
80	  clean global count of 2–50-dev shops exists — open question).
81	- **What they do today**: a shared config repo whose CLAUDE.md is copied or
82	  symlinked into each client project; layered global/client/project configs;
83	  how-to content explicitly targets multi-client Claude Code setups, and
84	  paid Gumroad packs are marketed to "agencies shipping the same stack
85	  across multiple client projects." Consultancies already sell "configure
86	  Claude Code for your team" engagements — both a channel and a substitute.
87	- **Documented demand for convergence**: anthropics/claude-code #14467
88	  "[FEATURE] Organization-wide shared CLAUDE.md via GitHub org" — open, 40 👍
89	  (verified 2026-07-31). Anthropic has not shipped it.
90	- **Trigger moment**: onboarding a new client repo or a new hire; a
91	  convention fix that must reach every client repo.
92	- **Willingness to pay**: the $100/seat gap between Claude Team Standard
93	  ($25) and Premium ($125, the Claude Code seat) normalizes per-seat spend
94	  for Claude-Code-attached capability. Realistic band: ~$20–50/seat/mo or
95	  $199–499/yr flat per org.
96	- **What matters in Claudinite's shape**: no server/account (client-repo
97	  security objections vanish — nothing of the client's leaves their repos),
98	  PR-gated automation (client-visible review trail), and per-client canon
99	  separation.
100	
101	## Segment: large enterprises (100+ engineers)
102	
103	- **Who buys**: platform-engineering/DevEx teams — Gartner: 80% of large
104	  software-engineering orgs will have platform teams by 2026 (up from 45% in
105	  2022); DORA: 90% of orgs have at least one internal platform. DX's survey
106	  of budget holders: 38% spent $101–500 per developer per year on AI dev
107	  tools in 2025; about half reserve 1–3% of engineering budget for AI
108	  tooling. Booking.com's DevEx team is the documented example of the buying
109	  center (procures AI tools, justifies with DX telemetry).
110	- **Scale of rollouts**: Uber ~90% of engineers on Cursor/Claude Code with
111	  in-house uReview gating; Accenture ~12,000 devs on Copilot; Infosys
112	  ~18,000; TELUS 57,000 employees on Claude; DX's Q4-2025 dataset (135k
113	  developers, 435 companies): 91% adoption, 22% of merged code AI-authored,
114	  and enterprises deploying "access controls, logging, approved model
115	  policies, and CI policy gates — not simply open access."
116	- **The precedent they hold**: Spotify's Fleet Management created 270,000+
117	  automated PRs across thousands of repos in 2022, 77% automerged — and its
118	  2025 Honk background agent (1,500+ merged AI PRs) rides the same
119	  infrastructure with CI/test gating and constraints on what the agent may
120	  touch. Puppet/Chef desired-state convergence is the older mental model:
121	  agents check in, compare to desired state, remediate drift. "Puppet for
122	  agent conventions, converging via reviewable PRs" is legible to any
123	  platform team.
124	- **Segmentation note**: the top ~20% (DORA "harmonious high-achievers" —
125	  the Ubers and Spotifys) build this in-house; the bottom ~10% lack
126	  prerequisites; the middle majority with partial practices that AI
127	  destabilizes is the addressable market.
128	- **Enterprises already accept the mechanism**: Claude Code managed-settings
129	  are deployed via MDM as non-overridable, file-based, no-server policy —
130	  proving appetite for exactly Claudinite's delivery shape at the
131	  device-policy layer (conventions/checks/fleet convergence remain
132	  unclaimed).
133	- **Ranked requirements a sale would face** (each grounded in the research;
134	  hardest first): (1) security/supply-chain review — SOC 2 or a compensating
135	  no-server data-flow story; reviews add 2–4 weeks and 77% of buyers demand
136	  verified compliance proof, though "code never leaves our environment" is a
137	  documented approval accelerant; (2) multi-agent support — enterprises run
138	  Copilot + Cursor + Claude Code simultaneously and converge on AGENTS.md,
139	  so Claude-Code-only addresses a slice of the fleet — and this near-blocker
140	  is now the best-quantified demand signal in the whole research set:
141	  `anthropics/claude-code` #6235 "Feature Request: Support AGENTS.md."
142	  ran from 2025-08-21 to its `completed` close on 2026-08-17 carrying
143	  4,944 👍 (6,367 total reactions, 374 comments), with #31005 (277 👍) and
144	  #34235 (90 👍) behind it — and it closed on the `/import` command while
145	  the Claude Code memory doc still states "Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`,
146	  not `AGENTS.md`" (re-verified 2026-08-21, Market wiki). That is roughly 100×
147	  the org-wide-shared-CLAUDE.md request (#14467, 40 👍) cited for the agency
148	  segment above, and the reaction base is the whole Claude Code user
149	  population rather than enterprise buyers specifically — so multi-agent
150	  emission reads as broad table stakes, not an enterprise-only gate;
151	  (3) private canon in
152	  the customer's own tenancy; (4) central non-overridable enforcement with
153	  an audit trail; (5) adoption/convergence metrics for the champion's ROI
154	  slide; (6) support SLA and vendor-viability mitigation (vendored plain
155	  files are a built-in escrow: they keep working if the vendor dies);
156	  (7) SSO — moot while there is truly no server, mandatory the moment any
157	  dashboard exists; (8) EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF mapping — a differentiator,
158	  not a burden: deployers' main in-force obligation is AI literacy, and a
159	  distributed, codified AI stance is the natural compliance artifact.
160	- **Regulatory tailwind**: under the EU AI Act, enterprises using coding
161	  assistants are "deployers" (model obligations fall on providers); NIST's
162	  RMF ecosystem pushes documented AI governance. Both reward "clear,
163	  codified, distributed AI stance" — which is what packs operationalize.
164	
165	## Sources
166	
167	- [Stack Overflow 2025 Developer Survey — AI](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) and [press release](https://stackoverflow.co/company/press/archive/stack-overflow-2025-developer-survey/) — 84%, 46%, 66% (via quoted context; survey site blocked direct fetch)
168	- [SO 2025 for leaders: AI agents](https://stackoverflow.co/teams/resources/2025-stack-overflow-developer-survey-for-leaders/ai-agents/) and [Agents on a leash — SO blog](https://stackoverflow.blog/2026/05/27/agents-on-a-leash-agentic-ai-remains-mostly-monitored-at-work/)
169	- [Announcing the 2025 DORA report — Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/announcing-the-2025-dora-report) — 90% use, amplifier finding; [trust breakdown](https://dora.dev/insights/balancing-ai-tensions/); [AI Capabilities Model](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/introducing-doras-inaugural-ai-capabilities-model); [RedMonk read](https://redmonk.com/rstephens/2025/12/18/dora2025/); [profiles — Faros](https://www.faros.ai/blog/key-takeaways-from-the-dora-report-2025)
170	- [Which AI coding tools do developers actually use at work? — JetBrains](https://blog.jetbrains.com/research/2026/04/which-ai-coding-tools-do-developers-actually-use-at-work/) — Claude Code 18%, CSAT 91; [State of Developer Ecosystem 2025](https://blog.jetbrains.com/research/2025/10/state-of-developer-ecosystem-2025/)
171	- [Anthropic acquires Bun; Claude Code reaches $1B](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-acquires-bun-as-claude-code-reaches-usd1b-milestone) (page proxy-blocked; milestone corroborated by [VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/technology/anthropic-says-it-hit-a-30-billion-revenue-run-rate-after-crazy-80x-growth))
172	- [anthropics/claude-code #18660](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/18660), [#34132](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/34132), [#14467 (org-wide shared CLAUDE.md, 40 👍)](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/14467) — verified via GitHub API 2026-07-31; ["It ignored them all" — dev.to](https://dev.to/minatoplanb/i-wrote-200-lines-of-rules-for-claude-code-it-ignored-them-all-4639)
